profile.name: Jackson Satermo

portrait.alt: Jackson Satermo smiling in a white shirt outdoors.

bio: I'm a software engineer who enjoys turning complex problems into thoughtful, useful experiences on the web. I'm drawn to the intersection of good design and solid engineering — where the details make all the difference.

These days, I'm a Programmer Analyst at the North Dakota University System, working across web development, PeopleSoft, PeopleTools, PeopleCode, and SQL. I earned my bachelor's degree from North Dakota State University in May 2025, and I'm excited to keep learning by building things that matter.

Away from my keyboard, you'll usually find me playing sports, leading a large Bible study, or tinkering with a 3D printer and modifying electronics. My faith, my community, and an active life keep me grounded — and give me plenty of ideas for what to build next.

aboutPhotos.alt: Jackson’s Bible study group gathered in a large circle at church.
aboutPhotos.caption: Faith, friendship, and a place to belong. The Bible study community I’m grateful to lead.

experience.description: Develop and support web applications for the North Dakota University System. Work with PeopleSoft, PeopleTools, and PeopleCode, with extensive hands-on SQL experience to support the systems people rely on every day.

projects.title: Everyday Progress
projects.description: A home for the habits that helped me lose 100 lbs through diet and exercise, without GLP-1s. Sharing my journey, progress photos, go-to recipes, and practical training tips to help others find their own way forward.

projects.title: Many Rooms
projects.description: Inspired by the idea of a place for everyone—and my experience coordinating 70+ church volunteers—Many Rooms is a concept for simpler church life. It would bring schedules, team coordination, and group messaging into one place, with text-message “Accept” or “Decline” replies for volunteers without smartphones and shared conversations to help leaders resolve scheduling conflicts.
